clue.text: A number of us do clubs — Kylie with short hot pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters before it are treated as a mess to be rearranged
short means the word hot loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A gossip item: some of us go clubbing, with Kylie Minogue in tiny hot pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims HOT to HO; 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) shuffles US DO CLUBS KYLIE plus HO into the Kylie Minogue hit of 1987.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song, and this is the title of Kylie Minogue's breakthrough pop single.

clue.text: Apple computer over time to retain power for crash

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next
to retain means the computer's name holds the next letter within it

parts.note: the iMac is a desktop computer made by Apple
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An Apple machine that keeps power over time, mentioned in a report about a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a violent collision, and an impact is the forceful striking of one body against another.

clue.text: Clean and polish stone

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or polish a blade or skill
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Instructions to wash and polish a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean in the sense of upright and free of wrongdoing, as in a clean record or a clean player.

clue.text: Get down, get up

parts.note: down and under both mean below or beneath
to get up is to rise to one's feet, to stand

explanation.surface: Two contradictory orders, as from a fitness instructor: get down, get up.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to grasp or comprehend it, as in 'I get it'.

clue.text: Charge from sex channel, turned over first

indicators.note: first says the flipped channel comes before the other piece
turned over means the word for channel is flipped so it reads the other way

parts.note: a bed is the channel a river runs in
IT is a familiar euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: A charge on a bill from an adult TV channel, which someone has quickly turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit is a sum charged against an account, the entry recording money owed.

clue.text: Writes book splitting section with prayers

parts.note: S is short for section, as in the § sign

indicators.note: splitting means the book letter breaks the following words apart by sitting inside them

parts.note: cries are pleas or appeals, prayers for help

explanation.surface: Someone writes, with a book dividing a section full of prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: Writes is a plural noun here: scribes are people who write, copyists or clerks.

clue.text: Tiger seen roaming the plain

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A tiger was spotted wandering across the grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: Tigers do not live on the Serengeti, which is African; a nice false note in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is the vast grassland plain of Tanzania, famous for its wildlife migrations.

clue.text: Horse went round circuit

indicators.note: round means the word for went goes around the circuit's letter

parts.note: ran is a past tense of go, as in went or travelled
O is a circle, a circuit or round shape

explanation.surface: A racehorse went round the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat has white hairs mixed through the base colour.

clue.text: Encouraging singer after critical review?

indicators.note: after puts the singer's name behind the critical reaction

parts.note: a boo is a jeer, a very critical audience response
Sting is the British singer, formerly of The Police

explanation.surface: Supporting a singer after a harsh review.
explanation.definitionFit: Boosting means lifting or promoting something, giving it a push of support.

clue.text: Take out daughter — endless party is extremely sleazy

parts.note: to see someone is to date or take them out

indicators.note: endless means the word for party loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: a fiesta is a party or festival

explanation.surface: Taking your daughter out to a party that never ends is about as sordid as it gets.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means squalid and disreputable, so the superlative form is the most sleazy.

clue.text: Puzzle not filled in and cryptic, having small squares

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters are jumbled
not filled in means the puzzle word is left with only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A crossword: a blank, cryptic puzzle with its little squares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not filled in' leaves PE from Puzzle; 'cryptic' then shuffles PE with AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A window with panes is divided into small glass squares, so it is described as paned.

clue.text: Song is simple: sing parts

indicators.note: parts means the word for simple is split open to take the singing word

parts.note: bare means plain or simple
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: A choir director's tip: the song is easy, just sing the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a boating song of the Venetian gondoliers, or music in that rhythm.

clue.text: Making ineffective players score

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors or players in a show
a rating is a score or mark awarded

explanation.surface: Players who make little impact on the scoreboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrating, figuratively, means depriving of force or vigour, rendering powerless.

clue.text: Case of Julia ignoring odd parts after film

indicators.note: after puts the remaining letters behind the film

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

indicators.note: ignoring odd parts keeps only the letters in even positions of the name

explanation.surface: Julia's case, which she ignored, after a film.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or toiletries, a crossword staple.

clue.text: Snow? Unusually answered with hesitation

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A weather report: snow, unusually, answered with some hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Snow is Jon Snow, long-time presenter of Channel 4 News in Britain; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jon Snow read the news on British television, an example of a broadcaster presenting bulletins.

clue.text: Olympian on drug for sport

indicators.note: on places the athlete's name after the drug in this across answer

parts.note: a tablet is a pill, a dose of a drug
Jessica Ennis(-Hill) is a British heptathlete, Olympic champion in 2012

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete caught taking a drug to help in their sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ping-pong, played with bats over a net on a table, is an Olympic sport.

clue.text: See 1 across
Scraps while group is playing inside

indicators.note: inside puts the group and the playing word within the word for while

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as I walked'
a band is a musical group
on means being performed, as a show is on

explanation.surface: Someone discards things while the band plays indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap something is to give it up or drop it entirely, the same as relinquishing.

clue.text: Home and lay to rest with single men

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
I is the Roman numeral one, single
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A funeral at home, burial with a lone man and some other men.
explanation.definitionFit: Home in the sense of domestic or inland, as in the interior ministry versus foreign affairs.

clue.text: Mad relatives start to see cause for embarrassment? They're out of hand

definitions.text: cause for embarrassment? They're out of hand
definitions.note: a source of slip-ups and gaffes, and, punningly, what is peeled off fruit taken from a bunch, which growers call a hand

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
kin are family members

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Crazy relatives are about to see something embarrassing that has got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas grow in clusters called hands, so their peel literally comes out of a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Political banana skins are pitfalls that make people slip up and look foolish.

clue.text: Get along? Take home to cheat

parts.note: to take home a wage is to make that much money
to do someone is to swindle or cheat them

explanation.surface: A question about getting by, followed by advice to take something home in order to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To get along with limited means is to manage or cope with what you have.

clue.text: Drink up: right animal

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the drink is written from bottom to top

parts.note: beer is a drink
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A command to drink up, then an approving 'right' — at the zoo, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok, or rhebok, is a small grey South African antelope.

clue.text: Born and died as Miss

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name
D is the genealogical abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A biographical entry: a woman born and died unmarried, as a Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss someone is to feel the lack of them, to want or long for them.

clue.text: Large American volume by don that is unable to write

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the letters for that is wrap around the earlier pieces

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
liter is the American spelling of litre
at can mean by, as in at or by the door

explanation.surface: A huge American tome written by a university don who, ironically, cannot write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like an Oxford lecturer but is the verb meaning put on, so 'that is' is worn around everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone illiterate cannot read or write.

clue.text: Complaint with space for writer

parts.note: IBS, irritable bowel syndrome, is a medical complaint
an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A writer given extra room to air a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Sweet thing in bar

definitions.meaning: a sweet baked dessert such as a sponge or gateau
a block of something, as soap comes in a block

explanation.surface: A dessert offered in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sweet baked confection and a moulded block, as in soap, share the one word.

clue.text: Chaos: girl dancing for rich businessmen

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chaos as a girl dances for wealthy businessmen at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchs are tycoons, often Russian, who are wealthy enough to wield political power.

clue.text: Geek to go on date with bachelor

indicators.note: on puts the word for go after the date letter in this across answer

parts.note: to wee is a childish word for to go to the toilet
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees

explanation.surface: A nerd about to go on a date with a single man.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a dull, socially awkward person, much the same as a nerd.

clue.text: One pushing 60 is gutted outside treatment room

indicators.note: outside places the gutted number around the pushing word
gutted means the number written as a word has its insides removed

parts.note: sixty is the number 60 in words
an urger is someone who pushes or urges

explanation.surface: Someone nearly sixty is devastated outside the doctor's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One pushing 60' looks like an ageing person; 'gutted' looks like dismay but strips SIXTY to SY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a surgery is the room where a doctor or dentist sees patients.

clue.text: Broads here and not guys

parts.note: nor means and not
folk means people, guys

explanation.surface: A complaint: women here and not men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broads' looks like slang for women but is the Norfolk Broads, a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Broads are waterways lying chiefly in this English county.
